protocols.title: Accidental hypothermia (adult)
protocols.subject: emergency
protocols.summary: Core temperature below 35 degrees C. Handle gently, prevent further heat loss, stage by core temperature or the Swiss system, rewarm actively in moderate to severe cases, and send patients in or at risk of cardiac arrest to an ECPR centre. Below 30 degrees C, limit shocks to 3 and withhold adrenaline.
sources: Paal P, et al. Int J Environ Res Public Health 2022

protocols.title: Acute (decompensated) heart failure and pulmonary oedema
protocols.subject: cardiology
protocols.summary: Treat the precipitant, give oxygen or NIV for hypoxaemia and respiratory distress, IV loop diuretic at 1 to 2 times the oral dose (20 to 40 mg furosemide if naive) with natriuresis-guided escalation, IV nitrate if SBP is above 110 mmHg, and reserve inotropes for hypotension with hypoperfusion.

protocols.title: Acute angle-closure crisis (acute angle-closure glaucoma)
protocols.subject: ophthalmology-ent
protocols.summary: A painful red eye with blurred vision, haloes, a mid-dilated pupil and a stony-hard eye is acute angle closure until proven otherwise. Lower IOP immediately with acetazolamide 500 mg (IV if vomiting), topical aqueous suppressants and steroid, pilocarpine once IOP starts to fall, mannitol if needed, and arrange laser iridotomy in both eyes.

protocols.title: Acute aortic syndrome and aortic dissection
protocols.subject: cardiology
protocols.summary: Suspect aortic dissection in any severe abrupt chest, back or abdominal pain; use the ADD-RS with D-dimer and urgent CT angiography, give IV opioid and IV beta-blocker to heart rate below 60/min and SBP 100 to 120 mmHg, send type A for emergency surgery and treat uncomplicated type B medically with TEVAR for complications.

protocols.title: Acute appendicitis (adult)
protocols.subject: surgery-trauma
protocols.summary: Stratify risk with the AIR or Alvarado score, image intermediate-risk patients (ultrasound first, low-dose CT if negative), and perform laparoscopic appendicectomy within 24 hours with a single preoperative antibiotic dose; antibiotic-first treatment is an option for selected uncomplicated cases without an appendicolith (WSES 2020).

protocols.title: Acute asthma exacerbation (adult)
protocols.subject: respiratory
protocols.summary: Grade severity by speech, respiratory rate, SpO2 and PEF; give inhaled salbutamol (with ipratropium if moderate or severe), oxygen only if SpO2 is below 92% (target 92 to 95%), prednisolone 40 to 50 mg within 1 hour, IV magnesium for poor responders, and discharge on ICS-containing treatment with review in 2 to 7 days.

protocols.title: Acute bacterial meningitis (adult)
protocols.subject: infectious-disease
protocols.summary: Blood cultures, then IV ceftriaxone plus vancomycin with dexamethasone within 1 hour of arrival; add amoxicillin when Listeria is possible (age over 50, pregnancy, immunocompromise). Do the LP at once unless CT criteria are met, and never let imaging delay antibiotics.

protocols.title: Acute cholecystitis and acute cholangitis
protocols.subject: surgery-trauma
protocols.summary: Diagnose and grade severity with the Tokyo Guidelines 2018, resuscitate and start antibiotics, perform early laparoscopic cholecystectomy (within 7 days of admission and 10 days of symptoms) for cholecystitis, and arrange biliary drainage, usually ERCP, timed to cholangitis severity.

protocols.title: Acute compartment syndrome of the limb
protocols.subject: surgery-trauma
protocols.summary: Suspect it with pain out of proportion to the injury and pain on passive stretch; release every circumferential dressing and cast down to skin, measure compartment pressure when examination is unreliable (delta pressure below 30 mmHg is a warning), and perform immediate fasciotomy of all involved compartments once diagnosed (BOAST 2025).

protocols.title: Acute infectious diarrhoea and dysentery (adult)
protocols.subject: infectious-disease
protocols.summary: Rehydrate first (ORS, or Ringer lactate for severe dehydration). Most watery diarrhoea needs no stool test or antibiotic; treat cholera with dehydration, dysentery, severe travellers' diarrhoea and sepsis, preferring azithromycin where fluoroquinolone resistance is common.

protocols.title: Acute ischaemic stroke: thrombolysis and thrombectomy
protocols.subject: neurology
protocols.summary: Time-critical reperfusion: IV tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg (max 25 mg) or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg (max 90 mg) within 4.5 hours for disabling deficits with BP below 185/110 mmHg, thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion up to 24 hours in selected patients, then aspirin and stroke unit care.

protocols.title: Acute kidney injury (adult)
protocols.subject: nephrology
protocols.summary: Diagnose and stage AKI with KDIGO creatinine and urine output criteria, find the prerenal, renal or postrenal cause, restore volume with buffered crystalloid, stop nephrotoxins, and start dialysis for life-threatening complications refractory to medical therapy.

protocols.title: Acute liver failure
protocols.subject: gastroenterology
protocols.summary: INR 1.5 or more with any encephalopathy and no prior liver disease: contact a transplant centre early, give IV N-acetylcysteine (paracetamol and early-grade non-paracetamol ALF), move to ICU at grade 2 encephalopathy, protect against cerebral oedema (sodium 145 to 150 mmol/L, early CRRT for hyperammonaemia) and apply King's College criteria.
sources: US Acute Liver Failure Study Group 2009

protocols.title: Acute lower GI bleeding
protocols.subject: gastroenterology
protocols.summary: Classify by shock index; unstable patients (shock index above 1) get CT angiography then embolisation, stable patients are scored with Oakland (8 or less: outpatient investigation). Transfuse restrictively and perform non-urgent inpatient colonoscopy for major bleeds.

protocols.title: Acute migraine attack (adult)
protocols.subject: neurology
protocols.summary: Screen for secondary headache red flags, then treat in the ED with IV prochlorperazine or metoclopramide, an NSAID (ketorolac or dexketoprofen) or SC sumatriptan, consider a greater occipital nerve block, give dexamethasone to reduce recurrence, and avoid opioids.

protocols.title: Acute pancreatitis
protocols.subject: gastroenterology
protocols.summary: Diagnose with 2 of 3 criteria, grade severity by revised Atlanta (persistent organ failure over 48 hours = severe), give moderate goal-directed Ringer lactate, feed orally early, avoid prophylactic antibiotics, ERCP within 24 hours only for cholangitis, and cholecystectomy before discharge in mild gallstone pancreatitis.

protocols.title: Acute pericarditis
protocols.subject: cardiology
protocols.summary: Diagnose with 2 of 4 criteria (typical pain, rub, widespread ST elevation or PR depression, effusion), admit if red flags, otherwise treat as an outpatient with high-dose aspirin or an NSAID plus colchicine for 3 months, tapering by symptoms and CRP; avoid corticosteroids as first line.

protocols.title: Acute poisoning: general approach (adult)
protocols.subject: toxicology
protocols.summary: Resuscitate with an ABCDE approach and a bedside glucose, identify the toxidrome, give activated charcoal 50 g only within 1 hour to a patient with a protected airway after a significant adsorbable ingestion, give specific antidotes early, and consider enhanced elimination for selected poisons.

protocols.title: Acute pulmonary embolism: risk stratification and treatment
protocols.subject: cardiology
protocols.summary: Assess clinical probability, use D-dimer and CT pulmonary angiography, stratify by haemodynamic status, sPESI, RV dysfunction and troponin; give systemic thrombolysis plus UFH for high-risk (shocked) PE, anticoagulation with monitoring for intermediate risk, and early discharge on a DOAC for low risk.

protocols.title: Acute severe ulcerative colitis
protocols.subject: gastroenterology
protocols.summary: Truelove and Witts severe colitis: admit, exclude infection (C. difficile, CMV), start IV methylprednisolone 60 mg/day or hydrocortisone 100 mg 3 to 4 times daily with LMWH prophylaxis, assess on day 3 and give infliximab or ciclosporin rescue to non-responders, with early surgical review.

protocols.title: Acute upper GI bleeding (non-variceal)
protocols.subject: gastroenterology
protocols.summary: Resuscitate, risk-stratify with the Glasgow-Blatchford score (discharge if 0 to 1), transfuse restrictively (Hb below 7 g/dL, or below 8 g/dL with cardiovascular disease), endoscopy within 24 hours, then high-dose PPI for 72 hours after endoscopic haemostasis.

protocols.title: Acute variceal bleeding in cirrhosis
protocols.subject: gastroenterology
protocols.summary: Suspected variceal bleeding: start a vasoactive drug (terlipressin, octreotide or somatostatin) and IV ceftriaxone immediately, transfuse restrictively (Hb 7 to 8 g/dL), band ligation within 12 hours, pre-emptive TIPS for high-risk patients, then beta-blocker plus EVL.

protocols.title: Adrenal crisis
protocols.subject: endocrinology
protocols.summary: Suspect in anyone with adrenal insufficiency or current or recent glucocorticoid use who has unexplained shock, vomiting or collapse; give hydrocortisone 100 mg IV or IM at once, 1 L saline in the first hour, then 200 mg/24 hours, and prevent recurrence with sick-day rules and an emergency card.

protocols.title: Adult cardiac arrest (ALS/ACLS)
protocols.subject: emergency
protocols.summary: High-quality CPR with minimal interruptions, early defibrillation for VF/pVT, adrenaline 1 mg every 3 to 5 minutes (as soon as possible for non-shockable rhythms, after failed initial shocks for shockable rhythms), amiodarone or lidocaine for refractory VF/pVT, and an active search for reversible causes.

protocols.title: Anaemia in pregnancy: Anaemia Mukt Bharat protocol
protocols.subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
protocols.summary: Anaemia in pregnancy is Hb below 11 g/dL (below 10.5 in the second trimester, WHO 2024). Give daily IFA from the second trimester; treat mild or moderate anaemia with 2 IFA tablets daily; IV iron after the first trimester if oral iron fails or Hb is 5 to 6.9 g/dL up to 34 weeks; transfuse if Hb is below 5 or severe after 34 weeks.

protocols.title: Anaphylaxis (adults and children)
protocols.subject: emergency
protocols.summary: Give IM adrenaline into the anterolateral thigh at once (0.01 mg/kg, maximum 0.5 mg; adults 500 micrograms), repeat after 5 minutes if needed, lie the patient flat, give oxygen and IV fluid for shock, and start a low-dose adrenaline infusion if two doses fail. Antihistamines and steroids are not first-line.

protocols.title: Aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage (SAH)
protocols.subject: neurology
protocols.summary: Thunderclap headache needs CT, with LP if CT beyond 6 hours is negative; secure the aneurysm within 24 hours, avoid severe hypertension, hypotension and BP swings before securing, give oral nimodipine 60 mg every 4 hours for 21 days, keep euvolaemia and watch for delayed cerebral ischaemia on days 4 to 14.

protocols.title: Anticoagulant-associated bleeding: reversal
protocols.subject: haematology-oncology
protocols.summary: Classify the bleed; for major or critical-site bleeding stop the anticoagulant and reverse it: warfarin with vitamin K 5 to 10 mg IV plus 4-factor PCC dosed by INR, dabigatran with idarucizumab 5 g, factor Xa inhibitors with 4F-PCC (andexanet is largely unavailable), and heparins with protamine.

protocols.title: ARDS: lung-protective ventilation (adult)
protocols.subject: critical-care
protocols.summary: Ventilate ARDS with tidal volume 4 to 8 mL/kg predicted body weight (start at 6) and plateau pressure below 30 cmH2O, use higher PEEP in moderate to severe ARDS without prolonged recruitment manoeuvres, prone for 16 hours or more when PaO2/FiO2 stays below 150 mmHg, and consider corticosteroids, early neuromuscular blockade and VV-ECMO in selected patients.
sources: Matthay MA, et al. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2024

protocols.title: Ascites, SBP and hepatorenal syndrome in cirrhosis
protocols.subject: gastroenterology
protocols.summary: Tap every new or admitted ascites (SAAG, PMN count, protein, culture); treat with 2 g sodium diet and spironolactone plus furosemide (100:40); give albumin 6 to 8 g per litre after paracentesis over 5 L; treat SBP (PMN above 250) with antibiotics plus albumin 1.5 g/kg day 1 and 1 g/kg day 3; treat HRS-AKI with terlipressin plus albumin.

protocols.title: Asthma long-term management (adults and adolescents)
protocols.subject: respiratory
protocols.summary: Every adult or adolescent with asthma needs ICS-containing treatment. GINA 2026 prefers Track 1: as-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol (Steps 1 to 2), then ICS-formoterol maintenance and reliever therapy (Steps 3 to 5); step up only after checking technique and adherence, and step down after 3 months of good control.

protocols.title: Atrial fibrillation: rapid ventricular rate, rhythm control and anticoagulation
protocols.subject: cardiology
protocols.summary: Cardiovert immediately if unstable; otherwise control rate (initial target below 110/min) with a beta-blocker, diltiazem or verapamil (LVEF above 40%) or digoxin, delay cardioversion beyond 24 hours unless anticoagulated for 3 weeks or TOE-cleared, and anticoagulate with a DOAC when CHA2DS2-VA is 2 or more.

protocols.title: Blood transfusion: thresholds, components and acute reactions
protocols.subject: haematology-oncology
protocols.summary: Use restrictive red cell thresholds (Hb below 7 g/dL for most stable inpatients, 7.5 for cardiac surgery, 8 for orthopaedic surgery or cardiovascular disease), single units with reassessment, evidence-based platelet, plasma and cryoprecipitate triggers, and stop the transfusion at once if an acute reaction is suspected.

protocols.title: Bradycardia with a pulse (adult)
protocols.subject: emergency
protocols.summary: Treat bradycardia (usually below 50/min) urgently only when it causes cardiopulmonary compromise: support ABC, look for causes, give atropine 1 mg IV (repeat to 3 mg), then transcutaneous pacing or an adrenaline or dopamine infusion, and arrange transvenous pacing early for high-risk blocks.

protocols.title: Burns: initial assessment and fluid resuscitation
protocols.subject: surgery-trauma
protocols.summary: Stop the burning and cool with running water, secure the airway early if inhalation injury is suspected, estimate TBSA (rule of nines, Lund and Browder in children), start formal fluid resuscitation at 2 to 4 mL/kg/%TBSA titrated hourly to urine output, and refer early to a burns unit.

protocols.title: Candidaemia and invasive candidiasis (adult)
protocols.subject: infectious-disease
protocols.summary: Treat every Candida-positive blood culture: start an echinocandin, remove the central line, repeat cultures until negative, arrange a dilated eye examination, step down to fluconazole after 5 to 7 days if stable and susceptible, and treat for 14 days after the first negative culture.

protocols.title: Catheter-related bloodstream infection (adult)
protocols.subject: infectious-disease
protocols.summary: Take paired catheter and peripheral blood cultures, start vancomycin plus gram-negative cover guided by severity and local resistance, remove the catheter for S. aureus, Pseudomonas, Candida or complicated infection, and set duration by organism and complications.

protocols.title: Cellulitis, erysipelas and skin abscess (adult)
protocols.subject: infectious-disease
protocols.summary: Separate non-purulent cellulitis (streptococcal: beta-lactam, 5 days, extend only if not improving) from abscess (incision and drainage; MRSA-active antibiotic only with systemic signs or risk factors), and exclude necrotising infection early.

protocols.title: Chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF)
protocols.subject: cardiology
protocols.summary: Start all four foundational drug classes early (ARNI or ACE inhibitor or ARB, beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2 inhibitor), up-titrate every 1 to 2 weeks to target or highest tolerated doses with potassium and creatinine checks, use diuretics only for congestion, and add iron, devices or other agents where indicated.

protocols.title: Chronic kidney disease: evaluation and management (adult)
protocols.subject: nephrology
protocols.summary: Stage CKD by cause, GFR and albuminuria (KDIGO 2024), then slow progression with BP control, maximum tolerated ACE inhibitor or ARB, an SGLT2 inhibitor, finerenone in albuminuric type 2 diabetes and a statin, manage anaemia, acidosis and mineral bone disease, and refer on KDIGO criteria.

protocols.title: Clostridioides difficile infection (adult)
protocols.subject: infectious-disease
protocols.summary: Test only new unexplained diarrhoea (3 or more unformed stools in 24 hours), stop the inciting antibiotic, and treat with fidaxomicin 200 mg twice daily or oral vancomycin 125 mg four times daily for 10 days. Fulminant disease needs high-dose enteral vancomycin, IV metronidazole and early surgical review.

protocols.title: Convulsive status epilepticus
protocols.subject: neurology
protocols.summary: Seizure of 5 minutes or more: benzodiazepine within 5 to 20 minutes (IV lorazepam, IM or buccal midazolam), repeat once, then one second-line IV drug by 20 to 40 minutes (levetiracetam 60 mg/kg, fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg or valproate 40 mg/kg), then anaesthetic infusion with EEG for refractory status.

protocols.title: COPD exacerbation (adult)
protocols.subject: respiratory
protocols.summary: Controlled oxygen to SpO2 88 to 92%, short-acting bronchodilators, prednisolone 40 mg daily for 5 days, antibiotics for 5 days only when sputum is purulent or ventilation is needed, and NIV for respiratory acidosis (PaCO2 45 mmHg or more with pH 7.35 or less). Start LABA+LAMA before discharge.

protocols.title: COPD stable management (GOLD ABE)
protocols.subject: respiratory
protocols.summary: Confirm COPD with post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC below 0.7, classify into GOLD group A, B or E, start a bronchodilator (A) or LABA+LAMA (B and E), add ICS only for exacerbations with blood eosinophils of 100 cells/microL or more (initially if 300 or more), and give smoking cessation, vaccination and pulmonary rehabilitation to all.

protocols.title: COVID-19 (adult): severity-based treatment
protocols.subject: infectious-disease
protocols.summary: Grade severity by SpO2 and respiratory rate. Non-severe but high risk: nirmatrelvir-ritonavir within 5 days. Severe or critical: oxygen, dexamethasone 6 mg for up to 10 days, an IL-6 receptor blocker or baricitinib, and prophylactic-dose anticoagulation. No steroids or empirical antibiotics for non-severe disease.

protocols.title: Deep vein thrombosis of the leg: diagnosis and treatment
protocols.subject: cardiology
protocols.summary: Use the Wells score to choose D-dimer or compression ultrasound, treat confirmed proximal DVT at home when appropriate with a DOAC (preferred over warfarin) for at least 3 months, stop after 3 to 6 months if provoked by a transient factor, and consider indefinite treatment if unprovoked or with persistent risk.

protocols.title: Dengue: assessment and fluid management
protocols.subject: infectious-disease
protocols.summary: Classify as dengue without warning signs, with warning signs, or severe dengue. Give paracetamol and oral fluids, never NSAIDs. Use haematocrit-guided isotonic crystalloid boluses with stepwise tapering for warning signs and shock, stop IV fluids by 24 to 48 hours, and do not transfuse platelets prophylactically.

protocols.title: Diabetic ketoacidosis (adult)
protocols.subject: endocrinology
protocols.summary: Confirm DKA by glucose or known diabetes, ketones and acidosis; give crystalloid, check potassium before insulin, start fixed-rate IV insulin 0.1 units/kg/h, add dextrose when glucose falls below 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L) and continue insulin until ketoacidosis resolves.

protocols.title: Drowning (adults and children)
protocols.subject: emergency
protocols.summary: Drowning kills by hypoxia, so ventilation comes first: open the airway, give 5 initial rescue breaths (with oxygen if available), then standard CPR. After rescue, treat hypoxaemia with oxygen, CPAP/NIV or intubation with PEEP, manage hypothermia, and observe for delayed respiratory deterioration. Antibiotics and steroids are not routine.
sources: Pellegrino F, et al. Ital J Pediatr 2023

protocols.title: Dyslipidaemia: risk categories, LDL-C goals and lipid-lowering therapy
protocols.subject: cardiology
protocols.summary: Classify cardiovascular risk, set a risk-based LDL-C goal (below 55 mg/dL (1.4 mmol/L) with at least 50% reduction for very high risk), start a statin at the right intensity, then add ezetimibe and a PCSK9 inhibitor or inclisiran if not at goal; measure Lp(a) once and check lipids 4 to 12 weeks after each change.

protocols.title: Ectopic pregnancy (tubal): diagnosis and management
protocols.subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
protocols.summary: Suspect ectopic pregnancy in any woman of reproductive age with pain, bleeding or collapse and a positive pregnancy test. Unstable: resuscitate and operate. Stable: transvaginal scan plus serial hCG; single-dose methotrexate 50 mg/m2 for small unruptured ectopics with low hCG, surgery otherwise.

protocols.title: Epistaxis (nosebleed) in adults
protocols.subject: ophthalmology-ent
protocols.summary: Sit the patient up leaning forward and compress the soft lower nose firmly for at least 5 minutes, then clear clots, apply a topical vasoconstrictor, find the bleeding point and cauterise it; pack if the site cannot be seen or bleeding persists (resorbable packs if anticoagulated), and escalate posterior or refractory bleeds to ENT.
sources: Indian J Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2024

protocols.title: Febrile neutropenia (adult)
protocols.subject: haematology-oncology
protocols.summary: Fever (single oral 38.3°C, or 38.0°C for 1 hour) with ANC below 500 cells/mm3 is an emergency: cultures and an IV anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam within 1 hour, MASCC risk scoring (21 or more is low risk), vancomycin or antifungals only for specific indications, and oral outpatient therapy only for selected low-risk patients.

protocols.title: First unprovoked seizure (adult)
protocols.subject: neurology
protocols.summary: Confirm an epileptic seizure, exclude provoking causes (glucose, sodium, calcium, alcohol, drugs, infection), do an ECG and neuroimaging, arrange EEG and specialist review within 2 weeks, give driving and safety advice, and start antiseizure medication only when recurrence risk is high or the patient chooses.

protocols.title: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM): India DIPSI pathway
protocols.subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
protocols.summary: Test every pregnant woman with a single-step 75 g oral glucose load, fasting or not; GDM if the 2-hour plasma glucose is 140 mg/dL (7.8 mmol/L) or more. Start MNT and exercise for 2 weeks, then add insulin (any gestation) or metformin (from 20 weeks) if 2-hour PPBS stays 120 mg/dL (6.7 mmol/L) or more.

protocols.title: Giant cell arteritis (GCA): urgent assessment and treatment
protocols.subject: rheumatology-dermatology
protocols.summary: In anyone aged 50 or over with new headache, jaw claudication, scalp tenderness or visual symptoms and raised ESR or CRP, start prednisolone 40 to 60 mg at once (IV methylprednisolone if vision is threatened), refer the same day, confirm by temporal and axillary ultrasound or biopsy, and consider tocilizumab to spare steroids.

protocols.title: Gout: acute flare and urate-lowering therapy
protocols.subject: rheumatology-dermatology
protocols.summary: Treat a flare early with low-dose colchicine, an NSAID or a glucocorticoid (prednisolone 30 to 35 mg daily for 5 days, or intra-articular). When indicated, start allopurinol at 100 mg/day or less (lower in CKD) and titrate to serum urate below 6 mg/dL, with 3 to 6 months of flare prophylaxis.

protocols.title: Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS)
protocols.subject: neurology
protocols.summary: Rapidly progressive, fairly symmetrical weakness with areflexia: monitor FVC and bulbar function closely (20/30/40 rule), treat patients unable to walk unaided with IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (within 2 weeks) or plasma exchange (within 4 weeks), and watch for dysautonomia.

protocols.title: Heat stroke (adults and children)
protocols.subject: emergency
protocols.summary: Core temperature above 40 degrees C with CNS dysfunction after heat exposure or exertion is heat stroke: cool first, transport second. Start whole-body cooling within 30 minutes (cold-water immersion for exertional cases, evaporative plus ice for frail classic cases) to 38 to 39 degrees C, then support failing organs. Antipyretics do not work.

protocols.title: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT)
protocols.subject: haematology-oncology
protocols.summary: Calculate the 4Ts score; if intermediate or high, stop all heparin and start a non-heparin anticoagulant (argatroban, bivalirudin, fondaparinux or a DOAC) while testing for PF4/heparin antibodies. Avoid warfarin until platelets recover and avoid routine platelet transfusion.

protocols.title: Hepatic encephalopathy in cirrhosis
protocols.subject: gastroenterology
protocols.summary: Grade with West Haven, protect the airway in grade 3 to 4, search for and treat precipitants (infection, bleeding, constipation, electrolytes, sedatives), give lactulose to 2 to 3 soft stools a day with early rifaximin, and continue secondary prophylaxis after the first episode.

protocols.title: Herpes zoster (shingles), adult
protocols.subject: infectious-disease
protocols.summary: Start oral valaciclovir, aciclovir or famciclovir within 72 hours of rash onset (later if new lesions, eye or ear involvement, or immunocompromise), refer ophthalmic zoster urgently, give IV aciclovir for disseminated, CNS or severe immunocompromised disease, and offer recombinant zoster vaccine.

protocols.title: HIV post-exposure prophylaxis and hepatitis B exposure (adult)
protocols.subject: infectious-disease
protocols.summary: After a significant exposure, give first aid and start TLD (tenofovir DF, lamivudine, dolutegravir) one tablet daily for 28 days as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours; test at baseline and follow-up, and manage hepatitis B by vaccination and anti-HBs status.

protocols.title: Hypercalcaemia (adult)
protocols.subject: nephrology
protocols.summary: Rehydrate with IV 0.9% saline, stop calcium-raising drugs, give zoledronic acid or denosumab for hypercalcaemia of malignancy (adding calcitonin when severe), and use PTH to separate PTH-mediated from PTH-independent causes.

protocols.title: Hyperkalaemia: acute management (adult)
protocols.subject: nephrology
protocols.summary: Protect the heart with IV calcium when the ECG shows changes, shift potassium into cells with insulin-glucose and nebulised salbutamol, remove potassium with binders or dialysis, and monitor glucose closely to prevent hypoglycaemia (UKKA 2023).

protocols.title: Hypernatraemia (adult)
protocols.subject: nephrology
protocols.summary: Restore circulation first if shocked, then replace the free water deficit with enteral water or hypotonic IV fluid, lowering sodium by about 10 mmol/L per day in chronic cases and faster in acute salt loading, while treating the cause and ongoing losses.
sources: N Engl J Med (Adrogue and Madias) 2000

protocols.title: Hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state (adult)
protocols.subject: endocrinology
protocols.summary: Restore volume with 0.9% saline first, lower osmolality slowly (3 to 8 mOsm/kg/h), start low-dose insulin 0.05 units/kg/h only once glucose stops falling with fluids (earlier if ketonaemic), and give LMWH and foot protection.

protocols.title: Hypertension: diagnosis and outpatient management
protocols.subject: cardiology
protocols.summary: Confirm raised office BP with home or ambulatory readings, assess cardiovascular risk and organ damage, start lifestyle measures, begin most patients with confirmed hypertension on a two-drug single-pill combination (RAS blocker with a calcium channel blocker or thiazide-like diuretic), and aim for SBP 120 to 129 mmHg if tolerated.

protocols.title: Hypertensive emergency and severe asymptomatic hypertension
protocols.subject: cardiology
protocols.summary: Hypertensive emergency is severe hypertension with acute organ damage: admit, use titratable IV drugs and lower BP to condition-specific targets (usually MAP down 20 to 25% over hours; immediately in aortic dissection, pulmonary oedema and ACS). Severe hypertension without organ damage is treated orally and gradually.

protocols.title: Hypocalcaemia (adult)
protocols.subject: nephrology
protocols.summary: Treat severe or symptomatic hypocalcaemia with 10 to 20 mL of 10% calcium gluconate IV over 10 minutes then a calcium gluconate infusion, correct magnesium, and treat the cause with oral calcium, active vitamin D or vitamin D repletion.

protocols.title: Hypoglycaemia in diabetes (adult)
protocols.subject: endocrinology
protocols.summary: Treat any glucose below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L): 15 to 20 g fast-acting glucose by mouth if alert, otherwise IV 10% or 20% glucose (or IM glucagon), recheck in 10 to 15 minutes, follow with longer-acting carbohydrate, and watch for recurrence with sulfonylureas.

protocols.title: Hypokalaemia (adult)
protocols.subject: nephrology
protocols.summary: Grade severity, check magnesium, replace orally when possible and give IV potassium chloride for severe, symptomatic or ECG-affected cases at no more than 10 mmol/h and 40 mmol/L peripherally, while treating the cause.

protocols.title: Hypomagnesaemia (adult)
protocols.subject: nephrology
protocols.summary: Give IV magnesium sulphate 1 to 2 g for arrhythmia, torsades or seizures followed by 4 to 8 g over 12 to 24 hours, use oral magnesium for mild deficiency, correct linked hypokalaemia and hypocalcaemia, and stop culprit drugs such as PPIs and diuretics.

protocols.title: Hyponatraemia (adult)
protocols.subject: nephrology
protocols.summary: Treat severe symptoms with 150 mL 3% saline boluses aiming for a 5 mmol/L rise, classify by osmolality and volume status, then correct by no more than 10 mmol/L in 24 hours (8 mmol/L in high ODS risk) and re-lower promptly if overcorrected.

protocols.title: Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) in adults
protocols.subject: haematology-oncology
protocols.summary: ITP is a diagnosis of exclusion. Treat newly diagnosed adults with platelets below 30 x 10^9/L or bleeding using prednisolone 0.5 to 2 mg/kg/day (6 weeks or less in total) or dexamethasone 40 mg daily for 4 days, add IVIg 1 g/kg for bleeding or when a rapid rise is needed, and escalate urgently for life-threatening bleeding.

protocols.title: Infective endocarditis: diagnosis, empirical therapy and surgery
protocols.subject: cardiology
protocols.summary: Take 3 sets of blood cultures before antibiotics, image with TTE then TOE, apply the 2023 ESC modified Duke criteria, start empirical IV antibiotics by setting (native or late prosthetic versus early prosthetic or healthcare-associated), and involve an Endocarditis Team early for surgery indications: heart failure, uncontrolled infection and embolic risk.

protocols.title: Inpatient hyperglycaemia and perioperative glucose management
protocols.subject: endocrinology
protocols.summary: Treat persistent glucose of 180 mg/dL (10 mmol/L) or more with scheduled insulin (basal plus prandial plus correction if eating, basal plus correction if not), aiming for 100 to 180 mg/dL on wards and 140 to 180 mg/dL in ICU, avoid sliding scale alone, and match insulin to steroids and surgery.

protocols.title: Iron deficiency anaemia (adult)
protocols.subject: haematology-oncology
protocols.summary: Confirm iron deficiency with ferritin (below 15 micrograms/L diagnostic, below 45 suggestive, higher with inflammation), start once-daily or alternate-day oral iron, switch to IV iron if oral fails or is unsuitable, and always find the cause, including bidirectional endoscopy in men and postmenopausal women.

protocols.title: Leptospirosis (adult)
protocols.subject: infectious-disease
protocols.summary: Suspect in fever with myalgia, calf tenderness or conjunctival suffusion after flood-water, field or animal exposure. Treat empirically: doxycycline for mild disease; IV penicillin or ceftriaxone for severe disease. Refer early for AKI, jaundice, bleeding or breathlessness, as pulmonary haemorrhage kills within hours.

protocols.title: Local anaesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST)
protocols.subject: anaesthesia
protocols.summary: Stop the injection, call for help, secure the airway with 100% oxygen, treat seizures with a benzodiazepine, give 20% lipid emulsion early (1.5 mL/kg bolus then 0.25 mL/kg/min under 70 kg), and run modified resuscitation with small adrenaline doses and no vasopressin or lidocaine.
sources: Local and Regional Anesthesia (El-Boghdadly, Pawa, Chin) 2018

protocols.title: Major haemorrhage in trauma (massive transfusion)
protocols.subject: surgery-trauma
protocols.summary: Damage control resuscitation: stop the bleeding fast, activate the major haemorrhage protocol, replace crystalloid with blood products in a high plasma ratio, give tranexamic acid within 3 hours, accept permissive hypotension, and correct fibrinogen, platelets, calcium and temperature guided by lab or viscoelastic tests.
sources: European Task Force for Advanced Bleeding Care in Trauma 2023

protocols.title: Malaria: uncomplicated and severe (India)
protocols.subject: infectious-disease
protocols.summary: Confirm every case by microscopy or RDT. Vivax: chloroquine 3 days plus primaquine 0.25 mg/kg for 14 days. Falciparum: ACT-AL in the North-East, ACT-SP elsewhere, plus single-dose primaquine. Severe malaria: IV artesunate 2.4 mg/kg (3 mg/kg under 20 kg) at 0, 12 and 24 hours, then daily.

protocols.title: Malignant hyperthermia crisis
protocols.subject: anaesthesia
protocols.summary: Suspect MH with unexplained rising end-tidal CO2, tachycardia and rigidity after a volatile agent or suxamethonium. Stop triggers, hyperventilate with 100% O2, give dantrolene 2 to 2.5 mg/kg IV every 10 minutes until controlled, cool, treat hyperkalaemia and acidosis, and monitor in critical care for at least 24 hours.

protocols.title: Metastatic spinal cord compression (MSCC)
protocols.subject: haematology-oncology
protocols.summary: In a person with cancer, back pain with neurological symptoms is an emergency: give dexamethasone 16 mg at once, immobilise if instability is suspected, get whole-spine MRI within 24 hours, and arrange surgery or radiotherapy (within 24 hours) through the oncology or MSCC team.

protocols.title: Myasthenic crisis
protocols.subject: neurology
protocols.summary: Myasthenic weakness threatening breathing or swallowing: monitor FVC and NIF serially in ICU, give plasma exchange or IVIg 2 g/kg, treat the trigger, stop drugs that worsen myasthenia, and hold pyridostigmine once intubated.

protocols.title: Myxoedema coma
protocols.subject: endocrinology
protocols.summary: Suspect in a hypothermic, drowsy patient with hypothyroidism and a precipitant; give stress-dose hydrocortisone and IV levothyroxine 200 to 400 mcg loading (100 to 200 mcg if older or cardiac), then 1.6 mcg/kg/day (75% if IV), with ICU supportive care and passive rewarming.

protocols.title: Necrotising soft tissue infection (necrotising fasciitis)
protocols.subject: surgery-trauma
protocols.summary: A clinical diagnosis driven by pain out of proportion and rapid progression: resuscitate, start broad-spectrum antibiotics including clindamycin or linezolid for toxin suppression, and take the patient for urgent radical debridement without waiting for imaging or scores, with planned re-look within 12 to 24 hours.

protocols.title: Non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTEMI and unstable angina)
protocols.subject: cardiology
protocols.summary: Confirm with serial high-sensitivity troponin, stratify risk, give aspirin and a parenteral anticoagulant, time angiography to risk (within 2 hours if very high risk, within 24 hours if high risk, otherwise selective), and use DAPT for 12 months by default.

protocols.title: Open fractures: emergency management
protocols.subject: surgery-trauma
protocols.summary: IV antibiotics within 1 hour of injury, tetanus prophylaxis, photograph then cover the wound with saline-soaked gauze and an occlusive film, realign and splint with repeated neurovascular checks, and arrange orthoplastic debridement: immediately if highly contaminated or ischaemic, within 12 hours if high-energy, otherwise within 24 hours.

protocols.title: Organophosphate and carbamate poisoning
protocols.subject: toxicology
protocols.summary: Resuscitate, then give atropine in doubling doses every 5 minutes until the chest is clear, heart rate is above 80 and systolic BP above 80 mmHg; maintain with an infusion of 10 to 20% of the loading dose per hour, consider pralidoxime, avoid routine lavage, and watch for intermediate syndrome.

protocols.title: Paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose
protocols.subject: toxicology
protocols.summary: Measure paracetamol at 4 hours or later and plot on the nomogram (US/Canada treatment line 150 mg/L, UK line 100 mg/L at 4 hours). Give IV acetylcysteine (at least 300 mg/kg over 20 to 24 hours, or the 12-hour SNAP regimen) ideally within 8 hours, and continue until stopping criteria are met.
sources: America's Poison Centers, AACT, ACMT, CAPCC 2023

protocols.title: Perioperative management of anticoagulants and antiplatelets (elective surgery)
protocols.subject: anaesthesia
protocols.summary: Classify thrombotic and bleeding risk, stop warfarin 5 days before surgery, stop DOACs 1 to 2 days before by bleeding risk and renal function (longer for dabigatran with low CrCl), avoid heparin bridging except in the highest thrombotic risk, continue aspirin in most cases, and respect neuraxial intervals.

protocols.title: Postpartum haemorrhage (PPH): first response and escalation
protocols.subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
protocols.summary: Measure blood loss objectively and act at 300 mL with an abnormal vital sign or at 500 mL. Start the whole first-response bundle within 15 minutes: uterine massage, IV oxytocin, tranexamic acid 1 g within 3 hours of birth, IV crystalloid, genital tract examination and escalation.

protocols.title: Pre-eclampsia, severe hypertension in pregnancy and eclampsia
protocols.subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
protocols.summary: Treat BP of 160/110 mmHg or more within 30 to 60 minutes (IV labetalol, oral nifedipine or IV hydralazine), give magnesium sulphate for severe features or eclampsia (Pritchard or Zuspan), and plan birth: 37 weeks without severe features, 34 weeks with severe features, after stabilisation for eclampsia.

protocols.title: Preterm labour and PPROM: corticosteroids, tocolysis and neuroprotection
protocols.subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
protocols.summary: If birth is likely within 7 days at 24 to 34 weeks and dating is reliable, give dexamethasone 6 mg IM 12-hourly x4. Use nifedipine tocolysis (24 to 33+6 weeks) only to complete steroids or allow transfer, magnesium sulphate before 32 weeks, erythromycin for PPROM and intrapartum GBS prophylaxis.

protocols.title: Rapid sequence induction and failed intubation (adult)
protocols.subject: anaesthesia
protocols.summary: Plan and brief before induction, preoxygenate head-up to an end-tidal O2 of 0.9, give an induction agent and a full dose of rocuronium or suxamethonium without delay, intubate with a videolaryngoscope, confirm with waveform capnography, and move promptly through DAS Plans A to D if intubation fails.

protocols.title: Rhabdomyolysis (adult)
protocols.subject: nephrology
protocols.summary: Confirm with CK above 5 times normal, start early isotonic crystalloid titrated to urine output 1 to 3 mL/kg/h (up to 300 mL/h), treat hyperkalaemia, look for compartment syndrome, and avoid routine bicarbonate, mannitol and diuretics.
sources: American Association for the Surgery of Trauma 2022

protocols.title: Scrub typhus
protocols.subject: infectious-disease
protocols.summary: Suspect in acute undifferentiated fever, especially with an eschar. Treat empirically without waiting for serology: doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days (azithromycin in pregnancy). For severe disease give IV doxycycline plus IV azithromycin for 7 days (INTREST).

protocols.title: Sepsis and septic shock: initial management
protocols.subject: critical-care
protocols.summary: Early recognition, cultures, antimicrobials within 1 hour for suspected septic shock or probable sepsis, 30 mL/kg crystalloid for hypoperfusion, noradrenaline to a MAP of 65 mmHg, and urgent source control.

protocols.title: Septic arthritis of a native joint (adult)
protocols.subject: surgery-trauma
protocols.summary: Treat an acute hot swollen joint as septic until proven otherwise: aspirate for Gram stain, culture and crystals and take blood cultures before antibiotics, start empirical IV antibiotics chosen by risk group, and drain the joint by repeated aspiration or arthroscopic or open washout.

protocols.title: Severe alcohol-associated hepatitis
protocols.subject: gastroenterology
protocols.summary: Diagnose clinically (NIAAA criteria), grade with MELD (above 20 severe) or Maddrey (32 or more), screen for infection, then give prednisolone 40 mg daily for 28 days (plus IV N-acetylcysteine for 5 days) if no contraindication; stop steroids if Lille score at day 7 is above 0.45. Nutrition and abstinence drive survival.

protocols.title: Sickle cell disease: vaso-occlusive crisis (adult)
protocols.subject: haematology-oncology
protocols.summary: Assess and give analgesia within 60 minutes of arrival, tailor opioids to the patient's previous needs and reassess every 30 to 60 minutes, give oxygen only if hypoxic, avoid overhydration, watch closely for acute chest syndrome, and start or optimise hydroxyurea.

protocols.title: Spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage (ICH)
protocols.subject: neurology
protocols.summary: Rapid CT diagnosis, early smooth systolic BP lowering to 140 mmHg (keep 130 to 150, avoid below 130), immediate anticoagulant reversal with PCC plus vitamin K or specific agents, and early neurosurgical referral for cerebellar haematoma, hydrocephalus or deterioration.

protocols.title: ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI): reperfusion
protocols.subject: cardiology
protocols.summary: Read the ECG within 10 minutes; primary PCI if it can be done within 120 minutes of diagnosis, otherwise fibrinolysis within 10 minutes and transfer for angiography at 2 to 24 hours (pharmacoinvasive), with aspirin, a P2Y12 inhibitor and a parenteral anticoagulant.

protocols.title: Surgical antibiotic prophylaxis (adult)
protocols.subject: surgery-trauma
protocols.summary: Give one IV dose of the right agent (usually cefazolin 2 g, 3 g if 120 kg or more) within 60 minutes before incision (120 minutes for vancomycin and fluoroquinolones), redose for long operations or blood loss over 1500 mL, and stop within 24 hours.

protocols.title: Syncope: initial evaluation and risk stratification
protocols.subject: cardiology
protocols.summary: Confirm true syncope, then do a history, examination with lying and standing BP, and ECG; identify high-risk features suggesting cardiac syncope needing admission or urgent evaluation, and discharge low-risk reflex or orthostatic syncope with education and follow-up.

protocols.title: Tachycardia with a pulse (adult)
protocols.subject: emergency
protocols.summary: Unstable tachyarrhythmia (usually 150/min or more with shock, altered mental state, ischaemic pain or acute heart failure) needs synchronised cardioversion under sedation. Stable patients are treated by QRS width and regularity: vagal manoeuvres and adenosine for regular narrow complex, rate control for AF, and antiarrhythmics or elective cardioversion for broad complex.

protocols.title: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP)
protocols.subject: haematology-oncology
protocols.summary: Suspect TTP in microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia with severe thrombocytopenia; send ADAMTS13 before treatment, use the PLASMIC score, start urgent plasma exchange with corticosteroids, add rituximab and caplacizumab where available, and avoid platelet transfusion unless bleeding is life-threatening.

protocols.title: Thyroid storm
protocols.subject: endocrinology
protocols.summary: Clinical diagnosis aided by the Burch-Wartofsky score (45 or more) or JTA/JES criteria; treat in HDU or ICU with beta-blockade, high-dose thionamide, iodine at least 1 hour after the thionamide, hydrocortisone, cooling and treatment of the precipitant.
sources: Japan Thyroid Association / Japan Endocrine Society 2016

protocols.title: Transient ischaemic attack (TIA)
protocols.subject: neurology
protocols.summary: Treat every suspected TIA as a stroke warning: aspirin immediately, same-day brain and vessel imaging and ECG, and aspirin plus clopidogrel for 21 days for high-risk TIA (ABCD2 4 or more) or minor stroke, started within 24 hours.

protocols.title: Trauma primary survey (xABCDE)
protocols.subject: surgery-trauma
protocols.summary: Team-based xABCDE primary survey (ATLS 11th edition): control exsanguinating external bleeding first, then airway with spinal protection, breathing, circulation with blood-based resuscitation and haemorrhage control, disability and exposure, treating each life threat as it is found before the secondary survey.
sources: European Task Force for Advanced Bleeding Care in Trauma 2023

protocols.title: Traumatic brain injury (adult): acute management
protocols.subject: surgery-trauma
protocols.summary: Classify by GCS, scan with CT using NICE 2023 criteria (derived from the Canadian CT Head Rule), prevent secondary brain injury by avoiding hypoxia and hypotension, give tranexamic acid within 3 hours for mild to moderate TBI, and treat raised ICP in tiers with early neurosurgical input.
sources: European Task Force for Advanced Bleeding Care in Trauma 2023

protocols.title: Tumour lysis syndrome (adult)
protocols.subject: haematology-oncology
protocols.summary: Risk-stratify every patient before anti-cancer therapy; hydrate and give allopurinol for low or intermediate risk, rasburicase for high risk or established TLS (after excluding G6PD deficiency), monitor electrolytes closely and involve renal and ICU teams early for dialysis.
sources: British Committee for Standards in Haematology 2015
Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust 2026

protocols.title: Type 2 diabetes: outpatient management
protocols.subject: endocrinology
protocols.summary: Aim for HbA1c below 7% in most adults, start metformin with lifestyle change, add SGLT2 inhibitors or GLP-1 RAs for ASCVD, heart failure, CKD or obesity irrespective of HbA1c, start basal insulin at 10 units or 0.1 to 0.2 units/kg when needed, and screen yearly for complications.

protocols.title: Urinary tract infection (adult): cystitis, pyelonephritis, complicated and catheter UTI
protocols.subject: infectious-disease
protocols.summary: Treat afebrile cystitis with nitrofurantoin or fosfomycin. For complicated UTI (fever, flank pain, systemic signs) culture first, choose empirical therapy by sepsis status, prior cultures and local resistance, switch to oral when improving and stop at 7 days in most. Do not treat asymptomatic bacteriuria.

protocols.title: VTE prophylaxis in medical inpatients
protocols.subject: haematology-oncology
protocols.summary: Assess VTE risk (Padua 4 or more, or IMPROVE 2 or more) and bleeding risk (IMPROVE bleeding 7 or more) on admission; give LMWH (preferred), fondaparinux or UFH to at-risk acutely or critically ill medical patients, mechanical prophylaxis when bleeding risk is high, and stop at discharge.

protocols.title: VTE prophylaxis in surgical patients
protocols.subject: anaesthesia
protocols.summary: Assess VTE and bleeding risk on admission (Caprini score), start mechanical prophylaxis, add LMWH or UFH when VTE risk outweighs bleeding risk, and extend prophylaxis to 28 days after major abdominal or pelvic cancer surgery and to 4 to 5 weeks after hip arthroplasty or hip fracture.
